entityDescription:
Compute Maritime is an innovation company providing AI-powered tools and solutions to help the maritime industry achieve its net-zero goals.

Our first tool in this effort is NeuralShipper™, the world’s first GenAI tool for ship design and optimisation. It is built on physics-informed diffusion and transformer models and trained on over 100,000 physically validated 3D ship hull designs across various ship types.NeuralShipper™ comprises three key modules: (I) design, (II) optimisation, and (III) simulation.

Our innovation lies in NeuralShipper’s design module, which integrates interactive and generative design capabilities into the preliminary design stage, enabling the creation of both customer-centred and high-performance designs. The generative design capability allows both experienced and novice ship designers to rapidly explore efficient design concepts. The interactive feature is particularly tailored for the yacht industry, where designs must be not only high-performing but also visually appealing.

In addition to design creation and optimisation, NeuralShipper™ enables users to develop machine learning-based surrogate models to bypass computationally expensive physical solvers for performance prediction. While surrogate modelling is not new, it has traditionally required strong machine-learning expertise. With NeuralShipper™, this process becomes straightforward, requiring only basic data and programming skills, making it easy for designers to get started.

We currently have four users on board. Among these, a key partner is Siemens, a leading provider of engineering design and simulation tools. The other users include two yacht design offices and MARIN, Europe’s largest research institution supporting the shipbuilding and offshore industries. Additionally, we are in discussions with well-known ship design firms, including Feadship, Delta Marine, and Damen.

entityDescription: Cerebri is committed to sustainable equality of care in the field of telemedical electroencephalography (EEG) diagnostics, so that an EEG will be possible for everyone, everywhere. At the same time, we are responding to the challenges of false-positive or false-negative findings and the lack of transparency and diversity of medical findings by providing specialized neurology specialists with years of experience and assisting artificial intelligence. With a location-independent telemedicine platform, Cerebri offers an innovative solution for broader availability and improved care.

HStar builds heavy-class, reusable spaceships and develops heavy-capable, global spaceports to sell launch services to customers around the world.

The HStar rocket is capable of unlocking the next phase of industry by deploying the biggest projects that will solve tomorrow’s problems on earth and accelerate many technological transitions.

HStar is a French-US initiative where both countries contribute to finance and build the global solution for worldwide application.

The HStar rocket uses proven technology which fills an undersupplied gap in the global launch market. It is an ITAR-free, non-dependent heavy launch capability using European very high thrust engines. A patent has been registered for France and Europe application.

HStar is a cohesive team with domain expertise building rockets and spacecraft. The company employs an experienced & proven team (eg. Kineis/CNES, SES, Eutelsat, ArianeGroup, SpaceX, NASA, etc). The team has developed a detailed, multi-horizon path to build Europe’s very heavy launcher, and then expand to sell global launch transportation services to the growing demand.

HStar leverages a public-private partnership model with key European partners and champions as well as European Member States to provide European response to US launch dominance. The distinct position among launch providers utilizes a lowest-risk, systems-integration approach. The company will provide global launch with spaceport partnerships, starting in French Guiana, the US, and Australia.

HStar has an accelerated path to first orbital launch in 2032, and launch services capable of one to two launches per week by 2036.

entityName: University of Zagreb Faculty of Geodesy - Chair of Satellite Geodesy
entityDescription:
The Chair of Satellite Geodesy is one of six departments within the Institute of Geomatics at the Faculty of Geodesy. Faculty members of the Chair include: Željko Bačić, PhD (Full Professor), Danijel Šugar, PhD (Associate Professor), Zvonimir Nevistić, PhD (Post.Doc researcher), Petar Jelić, MSc. (Assistant). 
The core areas of the Chair's activities cover all aspects of satellite positioning, space geodesy and geodetic astronomy, as well as the integration of space technologies with other sensors, and systems. The Chair’s educational activities are organized through seven compulsory and elective courses. At the undergraduate level: "Satellite Positioning", "Geodetic Astronomy" and “Engineering Informatics” and at the graduate level of Geodesy and Geoinformatics: "Navigation", "Integrated Systems in Geomatics", "Space Geodesy," "Satellite Geodesy - Project" and "Geodetic Astronomy - Project". 
The Chair's scientific and professional work focuses on the disciplines and courses it covers. In addition to these areas, Chair staff are actively involved in research on the application of GNSS for geodetic and non-geodetic purposes, investigating the effects of GNSS interference, monitoring the influence of the ionosphere on GNSS measurements, spatial data infrastructure, disaster risk reduction, drone applications, indoor navigation, application of spatial data in new concepts such as smart cities and digital twins and remote sensing.
The results of the Chair's work are reflected in a large number and wide range of published papers and participation in international and domestic conferences as well as leadership and participation in numerous scientific, professional, and educational projects (Erasmus+ CHBE and Strategic partnership). Chair staff lead and actively participate in the Copernicus Academy and Relay Croatia organizations and promoting space technologies in the Republic of Croatia through various channels.

entityDescription: Human in Motion Robotics (HMR) is a Canadian pioneer in developing next-generation exoskeleton technology rooted in advanced humanoid robotics and AI. entityName: Fondation Française pour la Recherche sur la Biodiversité
entityDescription:
The French Foundation for Biodiversity Research (FRB) is a platform between the various scientific actors and the society stakeholders on biodiversity.

The FRB was created in 2008, following the Grenelle de l’environnement (a series of political meetings organised in France in September and December 2007), on the initiative of the ministries in charge of research and ecology, by eight public research institutions. They have since been joined by LVMH, Ineris, the University of Montpellier and the French Biodiversity Agency (OFB), bringing the number of founding members to 11.

The Foundation’s mission is to support and act with research to increase and transfer knowledge about biodiversity. The FRB is a foundation for scientific cooperation under private law. It operates independently and has about 47 employees. The FRB has been headed by Hélène Soubelet since April 2017, with Denis Couvet as President since January 2021.
